newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's cereals harvest drops to 3.35 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's cereals harvest drops to 3.35 mln T.

text.p: Morocco expects its cereal harvest to drop by two-thirds to 3.35 million tonnes in 1996/97 frpm a record 10 million in 1995/96 season, due to bad weather, a Moroccan minister said on Wednesday.

Agriculture Minister Hassan Abou Ayoub told a news conference "heavy rains early this year and drought which hit later some agricultural areas" caused a dramatic drop in agriculture output, mainly cereals.
He said Morocco would have to import more soft wheat to meet demand.
"Morocco plans to import between 2.4 and 2.5 million tonnes of soft wheat in 1997/98 season, up from 1.1 million tonnes in 1996/97 season," Abou Ayoub told reporters.
"Cereals output, including soft and hard wheat and barley, will drop to 3.35 million tonnes in 1996/97 season against 10 million tonnes in 1995/96."
The cereals year runs for 12 months from around end-May/June.
Morocco imported 2.24 million tonnes of wheat from January to December 1996 and 2.54 million tonnes in calendar 1995.
Abou Ayoub estimated output as follows: 1.4 million tonnes of soft wheat, 0.7 million tonnes of hard wheat and 1.25 million of barley. He gave no figures for maize.

Last month, Finance Minister Mohammed Kabbaj said Morocco expected lower harvest to put the economy into "zero growth" by end 1997 compared with growth of 11.8 percent of GDP last year. Agriculture represents around 20 percent of GDP and employs nearly half the workforce. --Ali Bouzerda, newsroom +212-7 72 65 18
